name: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) v4.0
description: Compliance rules enforcing PCI-DSS v4.0 secure software development standards.

rules.title: SQL Injection Prevention
rules.summary: Bespoke and custom software must prevent injection flaws by using parameterized queries and stored procedures.
rules.description: SQL injection occurs when untrusted input is concatenated directly into SQL queries.

rules.title: Path Traversal Prevention
rules.summary: Software must validate user-supplied file path input against an authorized directory boundary.
rules.description: Path traversal occurs when untrusted user input controls file path resolution.

rules.title: OS Command Injection Prevention
rules.summary: Software must avoid executing operating system commands constructed from unvalidated input.
rules.description: OS command injection allows unauthorized execution of system commands.

rules.title: Strong Cryptography for Cardholder Data
rules.summary: Cardholder data must be protected using strong cryptography with acceptable key lengths and ciphers (e.g., AES-256).
rules.description: Legacy ciphers such as DES, 3DES, and RC4 are prohibited.

rules.title: Secure One-Way Cryptographic Hashes
rules.summary: One-way cryptographic hashes must use strong collision-resistant algorithms such as SHA-256.
rules.description: Weak hashes such as MD5 and SHA-1 must not be used for cryptographic protection.

rules.title: Cryptographically Strong Random Number Generation
rules.summary: Authentication tokens, session identifiers, and cryptographic keys must be generated using cryptographically secure pseudorandom number generators.
rules.description: Predictable random generators like java.util.Random and Math.random() must not be used for security tokens.
